_meanings:
‘The introducer’, an interlude acted by inferior characters
 (such as servants, buffoon <ab>&c.</ab>) for

 the purpose of acquainting the audience with events not represented on
 the stage, but a knowledge of which is essential for the proper understanding
 of what follows; (like the Viṣkambhaka it connects the story of the drama
 and the subdivisions of the plot, by briefly referring to what has occurred
 in the intervals of the acts, or what is likely to happen at the end;
 it never occurs at the beginning of the first act or at the end of the
 last). <ls>S. D.</ls> thus defines it:-- {#praveSako'nudAttoktyA nIcapAtraprayojitaH .#}
 {#aNkadvayAntarvijYeyaH SezaM vizkamBake yaTA ..#} <ls n="S. D.">309</ls>; see {#vizkamBaka#}; <ab>cf.</ab> <ls>Ve. 3</ls>.
